record.paper_title: Finite translation generalized quadrangles: old results, new results, open problems
record.original_question: If O(n, 2n, q) is a good egg in even characteristic—meaning there exists an element π such that for every two distinct other elements π′ and π′′, the space <π, π′, π′′> contains exactly q^n + 1 elements of the egg—is the egg necessarily regular?

evidence.quote: 3. Is any good egg O(n, 2n, q), q even, regular?
For n = m such a set O(n, m, q) is called a pseudo-ovoid or a generalized ovoid or an [n − 1]-ovoid or an egg of PG(2n + m − 1, q); a [0]-ovoid of PG(3, q) is just an ovoid of PG(3, q).

An egg O = O(n, 2n, q), respectively a TGQ T(O), is called good at an element π ∈ O if for every two distinct elements π and π′ of O − {π} the (3n − 1)-dimensional space < π, π′, π > contains exactly qn + 1 elements of O; in such a case π is called a good element of O.
Here, we speak of a regular pseudo-oval, respectively a regular pseudo-ovoid.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the projective space $\mathrm{PG}(4n-1,q)$ with $q$ even. An egg $\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}(n,2n,q)$ is a set of $q^{2n}+1$ pairwise disjoint $(n-1)$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathrm{PG}(4n-1,q)$ such that:
(i) any three of them span a $(3n-1)$-dimensional subspace, and
(ii) each element $\pi\in\mathcal{O}$ is contained in a unique $(3n-1)$-dimensional subspace $T_\pi$ (the tangent space) that is disjoint from every other element of $\mathcal{O}$.

The egg $\mathcal{O}$ is said to be good at an element $\pi\in\mathcal{O}$ if, for every two distinct elements $\pi',\pi''\in\mathcal{O}\setminus\{\pi\}$, the $(3n-1)$-dimensional subspace $\langle \pi,\pi',\pi''\rangle$ contains exactly $q^n+1$ elements of $\mathcal{O}$; in this case $\pi$ is called a good element and $\mathcal{O}$ is called a good egg.

The egg $\mathcal{O}$ is said to be regular (elementary) if there exists an $(n-1)$-spread $\mathcal{S}$ of some subspace of $\mathrm{PG}(4n-1,q)$ such that every element of $\mathcal{O}$ is a member of $\mathcal{S}$ (equivalently, $\mathcal{O}$ arises from a Desarguesian/elementary construction inside a $\mathrm{PG}(4n-1,q^{1/t})$-type configuration).

Question: Is every good egg $\mathcal{O}(n,2n,q)$ with $q$ even necessarily regular?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Lavrauw–Pavan, and later refinements showing pseudo-caps with two good elements are elementary) gives partial results but addresses primarily the odd characteristic case or stronger hypotheses (multiple good elements). No source found resolves the case of a single good element in even characteristic, and the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Characterisations of elementary pseudo-caps and good eggs
status_evidence.snippet: Improves the result that an egg with multiple good elements is elementary; does not settle the single-good-element case in even characteristic.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist but the even-characteristic case with one good element is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Translation Generalized Quadrangles in Even Characteristic
status_evidence.snippet: Studies TGQs and good eggs in characteristic two with various characterizations.
status_evidence.claim: Even-characteristic theory of good eggs studied; regularity of arbitrary good eggs not established.
